bandReport.notes:
COVERAGE. 11 items, 33-43, no gaps, none duplicated. Printed page numbers on my two pages read 19 and 21, consecutive odd numbers, so no English page falls between them and the even printed pages are the Hindi side. Both page keys in itemsByPage carry items; neither is empty. p18 opens with the 'Passage-4' heading, so nothing of item 33 is printed before my band, and p20 ends with item 43's four options, so nothing of it continues after. firstComplete and lastComplete are both true.

SHARED CONTEXT FOR ITEMS 43-48 - VERIFIED BYTE-IDENTICAL. p20-c2 prints 'Directions for the following 6 (six) items :', then 'Read the information given below and answer the six items that follow.', then the setup paragraph and the (i)-(v) clauses. Items 44-48 are on p22 and belong to band b4, which had already put that same setup in each of their context fields and flagged the two likeliest divergence points. I did NOT retype the setup: item 43's context is copied programmatically out of 2018-p2.b4.json item 44, so byte-identity is guaranteed by construction rather than by careful typing. sha256 of the shared context is c9ffefea1a9cc1c0f98ade39ccc16ff241f89c728fd54d00e9e7901beb762647 and it is identical across items 43, 44, 45, 46, 47 and 48.

I then read the copied text back against the p20-c2 column crop word by word, and specifically checked band b4's two flagged points. (i) 'Further, it is given that' ends in an EM DASH. Confirmed at 7x zoom off p20-c2: the mark is a full character wide, clearly longer than the hyphens elsewhere on the page, and matches the U+2014 in b4's file. (ii) The five sub-clauses (i)-(v) carry NO terminating punctuation. Confirmed at 2.8x zoom: no full stop, comma or semicolon on any of the five. THE PAGE AND THE SIBLING AGREE COMPLETELY - there is nothing for a human to adjudicate. The wording of the setup paragraph, the 'viz.,' abbreviations, the four parenthetical '(not necessarily in that order)' clauses and all five clause texts match the print exactly as b4 recorded them.

Per b4's convention the 'Directions ...' header and the 'Read the information given below ...' line are NOT in context; only the setup paragraph and the (i)-(v) list are, and the clauses are kept on their own lines.

PASSAGE-4 GOVERNS ONE ITEM. p18-c1 prints the 'Passage-4' heading, the passage, then item 33; the next item, 34, is a numeracy item with no passage. So the mapping here is one passage to one item, not a shared block. Following the shipped Paper II convention (documented by band b4 for its own eight single-item passages) the passage is still placed in context, and the 'Passage-4' label is not included. No hash collision results: item 33's stem and option set are unique in this band.

DECIMAL SEPARATOR. Not applicable to my band - there is no decimal number anywhere on p18 or p20. Every numeric value in items 33-43 is an integer, a percentage written with a whole number, or a vulgar fraction. So no U+00B7 middle dot was needed and none was introduced.

COLUMN CROPS. Both c1 crops are clean and complete. Both c2 crops carry a narrow bleed of the LEFT column's right edge down their far-left margin (stray letter fragments from the neighbouring column's line ends). That is cosmetic - it adds a sliver of the other column rather than removing anything from this one - and no item number or option block is cut. Nothing was read off the whole-page image except the printed page numbers and the overall column structure. Reading order was strictly all of c1 then all of c2 on each page.

TRANSCRIPTION CHOICES WORTH A SECOND EYE, each also flagged on its own item. (a) Item 37 compares words with < and > signs; those are left as plain text because the compared terms are ordinary words, and a scan of every shipped band file in scripts/upsc/data found no precedent in either direction. (b) Item 39 is a probability item and catalog.json has no probability chapter or subtopic under any CSAT subject; no shipped Paper II file contains a probability item either. It is filed under Basic Numeracy > Arithmetic Operations and Ratios with a new soft subtopic label 'Probability' - a genuine catalog gap, not a near-miss. (c) Item 40 wraps the person labels A and B as math zones, following b1 item 5 and b5 item 71 of this paper, while item 43 leaves the puzzle's A-D plain, following b4; each block therefore matches its own precedent. (d) Item 36's three possessives are printed with typographic apostrophes and are transcribed with the ASCII apostrophe, which is what b4 and b5 use throughout.

PAPER DEFECTS. None found. No duplicated option text, no item with a missing or blank option, no item number skipped, no arithmetic or spelling oddity in the printed text of these eleven items. Item 40's option (d) is the unreduced ratio 4 : 2, which is how it is printed and is a distractor rather than a defect. No item in this band needs a figure; every one is answerable from its printed text.

questions.context: Some people believe that leadership is a quality which you have at birth or not at all. This theory is false, for the art of leadership can be acquired and can indeed be taught. This discovery is made in time of war and the results achieved can surprise even the instructors. Faced with the alternatives of going left or right, every soldier soon grasps that a prompt decision either way is better than an endless discussion. A firm choice of direction has an even chance of being right while to do nothing will be almost certainly wrong.

questions.stem: A bag contains 15 red balls and 20 black balls. Each ball is numbered either 1 or 2 or 3. 20% of the red balls are numbered 1 and 40% of them are numbered 3. Similarly, among the black balls, 45% are numbered 2 and 30% are numbered 3. A boy picks a ball at random. He wins if the ball is red and numbered 3 or if it is black and numbered 1 or 2. What are the chances of his winning?
